US-AL.note: Participation is by application and acceptance (My Alabama Taxes) BEFORE collecting — the election is a fact about the seller, not a default. The 8% relieves both seller and purchaser of any other state or local sales/use tax on the transaction (§ 40-23-193(a), (c)), and no participating seller may be required to collect more regardless of the combined local rate. Statutory, no scheduled end; the base is tangible personal property delivered into Alabama — category taxability still gates first.

source.name: Ala. Code § 40-23-193(a),(c) (Code of Alabama 1975, 2024 ed.), agreeing with the Alabama DOR's Simplified Sellers Use Tax program page (rate, application requirement, monthly e-remittance)

US-TX.note: Elected by a remote seller via Form 01-799; replaces the LOCAL use taxes only — the 6.25% state rate still applies on top, for 8% combined. The figure is an ANNUAL redetermination published in the Texas Register by Jan 1, which is why this window closes with the calendar year: a build after 2026-12-31 without next year's determination drops the scheme, and a consumer that cannot find it must refuse to price under the election rather than assume the old figure.

source.name: Tex. Tax Code § 151.0595 with the Comptroller's Single Local Use Tax Rate pages; 1.75% for calendar 2026 determined from FY-2025 collections, announced 2025-12-26 in the Texas Register (Tax Policy News, January 2026)
